business.what: CreditAccess Grameen Ltd is India's largest NBFC-MFI that empowers women entrepreneurs and low-income households by providing flexible and responsible financial solutions. It makes money through interest and other charges on a wide range of group loans and retail loans, such as livelihood loans, retail finance, and housing loans, supported by diversified borrowings and cost-effective operations.

segments.name: Group Loans
segments.detail: Includes joint liability group (JLG) products such as livelihood loans, IGLG pragati loans, emergency loans, water loans, and sanitation loans.

segments.name: Retail Loans
segments.detail: Includes individual and retail finance products such as Unnati loans, Vikas loans, housing loans, and two-wheeler loans, reaching an AUM of ₹53.62 billion.

strategy: Strengthen the balance sheet, improve portfolio quality, and focus on sustainable business growth
Expand presence in the retail finance space through tailored products addressing diverse financial needs
Scale business guided by diligence, MFIN Guardrails, regulatory norms, and internal risk thresholds
Diversify the liability franchise and leverage technology for digital platforms like Mahi

narrative.read: CreditAccess Grameen has staged a dramatic operational turnaround, with quarterly Net Profit surging from a loss of ₹100 crore in Dec 2024 to ₹502 crore in Sep 2026. Financing Margin % expanded from -8% in Dec 2024 to 36% in Sep 2026 while Gross NPA % declined from 4.76% in Mar 2025 to 2.18% in Jun 2026.

narrative.credibility: Management demonstrated strong operational control by upgrading all major FY27 profitability targets (ROA, ROE, NIM, cost-to-income) in Q2 FY27, though reported financials trace generic line items rather than company-defined metrics.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Asset quality normalization and PAR accretion reduction driving operational turnaround.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Gross NPA % dropped continuously from a high of 4.76% in Mar 2025 to 2.18% in Jun 2026.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Strong rebound in bottom-line performance entering FY27.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Net Profit recovered from a loss of ₹100 crore in Dec 2024 to ₹493 crore in Jun 2026 and ₹502 crore in Sep 2026.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Top-line revenue expansion driven by business scaling.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Quarterly Revenue increased consistently from ₹1,380 crore in Dec 2024 to ₹1,904 crore in Sep 2026.

bull: Substantial expansion in quarterly Net Profit, rising from a loss of ₹100 crore in Dec 2024 to ₹502 crore in Sep 2026.
Strong recovery in Financing Margin %, expanding from -8% in Dec 2024 to 38% in Jun 2026 and 36% in Sep 2026.
Significant reduction in asset quality stress, with Gross NPA % declining from 4.76% in Mar 2025 to 2.18% in Jun 2026.
bear: Historical earnings vulnerability to credit cycles, reflected in annual Net Profit dropping from ₹1,446 crore in Mar 2024 to ₹531 crore in Mar 2025.
Potential credit cost pressure in H2 FY27 highlighted by management regarding drought conditions in Maharashtra and flood impacts in other operating states.
Lending rate reduction of 50 bps implemented in H2 FY27 could weigh on yield expectations if marginal borrowing costs escalate.
askManagement: How will the 50 bps lending rate cut impact NIM targets for H2 FY27 given rising marginal bank borrowing rates?
What is the quantitative impact of localized drought conditions in Maharashtra on H2 FY27 credit cost run rates?
As Retail Finance expands to 23.3% of total AUM, how do credit costs and write-offs in individual/secured loans compare to traditional joint liability group loans?
